notes.summary: Checked CLD v2 is the July 2025 version, not ordinal stage 2. GJR 15.11 gives weakly smooth nets; ordinary smoothness and sequence extraction require separate arguments. Checked local approximation yields stage 1 for LFS and stage 2 for interior semipositive real PL.
notes.detailedSummary: The actual CD Definition 8.1.1 and Lemma 8.1.4 start with ordinary smooth functions with positive d'd'' and use decreasing sequences for successor stages. The analytic refined G-tropical structure uses ordinary moment charts, and analytic/scalar pullbacks preserve each ordinal. GJR 15.11 requires a boundaryless rig-smooth curve and produces a decreasing net of weakly smooth psh functions. GJR 15.10 makes these ordinary smooth when the residue field is algebraic over a finite field, or the curve is potentially locally P1. GJR 7.10 has an interior hypothesis and a common ordinary open uniform LFS approximation; combined with explicit smooth maxima it safely gives stage 2 for semipositive real PL, without an unsupported flattening to stage 1.
notes.text:
These are checked published foundations and fresh stage bookkeeping, not a classification. CD denotes the supplied arXiv:1204.6277v2 PDF dated 25 July 2025. Definition 8.1.1 (p.195) defines the smallest ordinary subsheaf containing smooth functions q with d'd''q≥0 and stable under decreasing sequences. Lemma 8.1.4 (p.196) defines Psh_0 as these smooth functions, Psh_{α+1} by local decreasing sequential limits of Psh_α, and limit stages by local membership in an earlier stage. Thus 'v2' names the paper version; Psh_2 is an additional ordinal bound. Neither current positivity nor classical pshness alone gives this bound.

CD 12.4.1/12.4.6 equips Hausdorff analytic spaces with the analytic refined G-tropical structure. CD 15.1.1(b)/15.1.2 describes ordinary smooth functions by ordinary open local expressions φ(-log|g_1|,…,-log|g_r|), with analytic units and smooth φ. G-local real PL or harmonic tropicalizations cannot be substituted. CD 15.7.1 makes a pure-dimensional Hausdorff analytic space a tropical space with its actual analytic boundary; 15.7.2 records ∂V=(∂X∩V)∪∂(V/X). CD 12.4.5 and 8.1.5 preserve each ordinal stage under analytic morphisms, including scalar projections over different complete fields. CD 8.3.1(b) converts positive currents to positive d'd'' forms for smooth functions on boundaryless tropical spaces; this does not give such a conclusion for arbitrary functions.

GJR denotes the exact supplied arXiv:2111.05741. Its Definition 5.1 defines real PL using G-local real combinations of unit log norms. Definition 7.8 and 7.9 make LFS a semipositive real-PL class with ordinary local expressions as nonnegative linear combinations of finite maxima of negative log norms of units. Each such maximum has actual ordinary smooth decreasing approximants M_ε=ε log Σ exp(ℓ_i/ε) on its fixed ordinary moment neighborhood. They satisfy 0≤M_ε−max ℓ_i≤ε log N, and ∂M_ε/∂ε=−Σp_i log p_i≥0. Their Hessians are positive, so convex moment pullbacks have positive d'd''. Nonnegative finite sums preserve this construction. Therefore every LFS function lies locally in Psh_1, with genuine ordinary smooth sequences on a common ordinary neighborhood.

GJR Proposition 7.10 (pp.47–48) requires an interior point. Its proof produces the ordinary open tube U=red^{-1}(V') and LFS functions h_i converging uniformly there to a semipositive real-PL h. Choose a subsequence with ||h_{i_j}−h||_U≤e_j=4^{-j}, and put b_j=h_{i_j}+2e_j. Then h+e_j≤b_j≤h+3e_j and b_{j+1}≤h+3e_{j+1}<h+e_j≤b_j. Each b_j is stage 1 on U, so b_j↓h proves stage 2. Each inner ordinary smooth sequence has a fixed ordinary neighborhood, while the outer sequence is on U. A single smooth sequence on U approximating h is not proved; the two limits are not silently flattened.

GJR Proposition 15.11 (pp.80–81) assumes a smooth curve, explicitly meaning rig-smooth without boundary, and gives a decreasing net of weakly smooth psh functions on every relatively compact ordinary open subset. Remark 15.10 supplies equality of weak and ordinary smooth sheaves when the residue field is algebraic over a finite field, or the curve is potentially locally P1. Its Remark 10.10 identifies the ordinary smooth sheaf with CLD's ordinary sheaf. Restricting positive weak currents to ordinary tests and then using CD 8.3.1(b) verifies stage-0 positivity once ordinary smoothness is established. Outside those cases harmonic germs can be non-smooth; that observation is not proof that stage 1 or 2 fails.

Other checked foundations: GRc=arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September 2025, Theorem 4.3 identifies semipositive real PL and classical psh on good strict spaces over nontrivially valued fields; Definition 4.1 quantifies over every analytic field extension and curve morphism. Its Lemma 3.9 describes normalization over perfect fields; Theorems 6.1 and 6.4 give interior and Shilov maximum principles. In the supplied arXiv:2503.05513, the smooth-curve subharmonic real-PL/nef equivalence is Proposition 5.1, not the older Proposition 3.1 cited in GRc. Thuillier's supplied thesis Proposition 3.1.8(iii), printed p.62/PDF p.76, concerns an increasing locally bounded subharmonic family; Theorem 3.4.2 gives decreasing families of subharmonic Thuillier-lisse functions on relatively compact ordinary opens. Proposition 3.2.5 identifies these lisse functions as G-local real PL, not ordinary CLD-smooth.

Evidence and reproduction: six supplied PDF/text hash pairs matched. Seventy-five literal primary pages, including indispensable proof continuations, and checked applications are retained in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Actual PDF pages Thu 76, CD 196 and GJR 80 were visually inspected; the first actually says 'famille croissante et localement bornée', and GJR actually says 'decreasing net', 'weakly smooth', and 'without boundary'. Run python extract_sources.py and python render_sources.py. Rendering succeeded; Thu's renderer reported 156 Type-3 glyph bounding-box warnings, which are retained in source-extracts/render-diagnostics.json and the page renderer output. These are source observations and mathematical arguments using checked published foundations, not computational proof certificates.

notes.summary: Full-union envelopes have ordinary CLD stage 1 on boundaryless reduced good strict pure curves with bijective normalization over perfect countably dense fields whose residue is algebraic over a finite field. This includes positive-genus curves over Qp. Without the residue/genus condition the checked route gives only stage 3.
notes.detailedSummary: For every usc obstacle, including empty-family cases, the entire LFS/semipositive real-PL envelope is addressed. A baseline and finite maxima make the normalized family locally bounded on both sides; Thuillier's supremum theorem gives a subharmonic regularized envelope. A countable-topology lemma extracts sequences from continuous decreasing nets on a fixed ordinary neighborhood. Under the residue hypothesis, GJR's net is ordinary smooth, giving stage 1. Smooth approximants descend through homeomorphic normalization because they are locally constant at non-normal rigid points. Every analytic extension and curve pullback preserves the bound. No continuity or arbitrary scalar-envelope identity is asserted. Without ordinary/weak sheaf equality, decreasing real-PL regularization composed with the stage-2 lemma yields stage 3, not stage 2.
notes.text:
Theorem. Let K be complete, nontrivially valued and perfect, with a countable dense subset. Let X be a nonempty reduced, separated, good, strict K-analytic curve pure of dimension one, with ∂X=∅ and normalization ν:X̃→X bijective on Berkovich points. If the residue field K̃ is algebraic over a finite field, then for every usc f:X→R∪{−∞}, the usc regularization u of the supremum over the FULL real-valued locally-Fubini–Study/semipositive-real-PL minorant union belongs to Psh_{X,1}⊂Psh_{X,2}. Locally it is a decreasing sequence of finite ordinary CLD-smooth functions with positive d'd'' on one ordinary neighborhood. The same stage-1 conclusion holds under the alternative concrete hypothesis that X̃ is potentially locally P1. If neither residue/genus hypothesis is imposed, the following proof gives Psh_{X,3}, and does not establish Psh_{X,2}.

Proof of the full-family step. If the family is empty, the raw and regularized envelopes are −∞, with smooth approximants −j. Otherwise fix one member h_0. All competitors are finite continuous and classically psh by the checked LFS and GRc equivalences in n1. Thus f is finite everywhere and locally bounded above by usc. The regularization satisfies h_0≤s≤u≤f. The last inequality follows because f is itself usc and majorizes s. In particular u is finite. GRc Lemma 3.9 makes X̃ rig-smooth and boundaryless; ν is a topological quotient and hence, being bijective, a homeomorphism. Pulling the entire family back gives finite subharmonic functions on X̃. Direct finite subsets containing h_0 by inclusion and take their maxima. These maxima are subharmonic and are locally bounded both below by h_0∘ν and above by f∘ν. They need not be real PL; no real-PL maximum closure is assumed. Thuillier 3.1.8(iii) therefore makes (s∘ν)* subharmonic. Homeomorphic regularization gives (s∘ν)*=u∘ν. No selected family or modulus condition is used.

Sequence extraction. A strict K-affinoid algebra A is separable as a Banach space because countably many Tate polynomials with coefficients in a countable dense subset of K have dense images. Evaluations satisfy ||a(x)|−|b(x)||≤||a−b||. A countable norm-dense set of evaluations therefore separates points and generates the topology of M(A), embedding it in a countable product of compact real intervals. Consequently M(A) is second countable. A relatively compact ordinary open W in a good Hausdorff space is covered by finitely many interiors of affinoid neighborhoods of its compact closure, and is second countable. For a decreasing directed net a_i of continuous functions with infimum v on W, the sets {v<t}=⋃_i{a_i<t} are open and Lindelof. For each rational t choose a countable subcover; enumerate all selected indices and choose successively dominating indices. The resulting sequence decreases to v: a larger limit would contradict one rational threshold and its chosen covering index. This works on the SAME W, also when v takes −∞.

Stage 1. On a relatively compact ordinary neighborhood W̃ of the selected point of X̃, GJR 15.11 provides a decreasing net of finite weakly smooth psh functions converging to u∘ν. The residue-field assumption, or the stated potentially-local-P1 assumption, makes these ordinary smooth by GJR 15.10. Their positive ordinary currents give positive ordinary forms by CD 8.3.1(b). They are therefore stage 0, not just harmonic approximants. The extraction lemma yields an actual decreasing stage-0 sequence on W̃.

Ordinary descent. Normalization is an analytic isomorphism off a discrete set of non-normal rigid points. An ordinary smooth function is locally constant at any rigid point, including one with a finite residue extension. Indeed, for an analytic unit g at such a point z, let α=g(z), ρ=|α|>0, and let P be its monic minimal polynomial of degree d. All conjugate roots have modulus ρ because K is complete. On the ordinary neighborhood |P(g)|<ρ^d, if |g(y)|≠ρ then after algebraic extension of H(y) all root differences have modulus max(|g(y)|,ρ), so |P(g(y))|≥ρ^d, a contradiction. Thus |g| is locally constant; finitely many units in a smooth moment expression make the smooth function constant. Transfer each normalized smooth approximant through the homeomorphism. Off the non-normal points it is smooth and positive by analytic isomorphism; at those points it is constant on an ordinary neighborhood, so smooth with zero d'd''. Each transferred function is therefore stage 0 on W=ν(W̃), and their decreasing sequence converges to u. This proves stage 1. The same argument inductively descends the finite ordinal stages used here.

General residue fields. Thuillier 3.4.2 instead supplies a decreasing net of continuous subharmonic lisse functions on W̃. By Thuillier 3.2.5 these are real PL, and by the supplied GRs Proposition 5.1 they are semipositive. The interior approximation lemma in n1 puts each in stage 2. Extracting a decreasing sequence gives stage 3; descending the construction gives Psh_{X,3}. No nested-limit collapse to stage 2 is justified.

Scalar and curve quantifiers. For EVERY analytic extension K'/K, including nonseparable and larger-residue extensions, and every analytic curve morphism C→X_{K'}, CD 12.4.5/8.1.5 preserves the proved ordinal bound for u∘π∘g. Equivalently all ordinary smooth sequences in the construction can be pulled back. Smooth psh curve functions are subharmonic and decreasing limits remain so, as checked in GRc §1.2 and Proposition 3.5. This also proves classical pshness in its scalar-stable extended convention. No assertion that (s∘π)*=s*∘π or that the enlarged full competitor family has the same envelope is made or needed.

This is a noninvariant full-envelope sector: it applies to all ordinary open boundaryless domains in smooth elliptic and higher-genus curves over Qp, not just to rational trees or toric competitors. There is no continuity assertion for usc obstacles. The perfect/countability/residue hypotheses are sufficient, not proved necessary. Boundary points and ordinary approximation descent from arbitrary completed perfect closures remain outside the theorem.

The entire proof, exact foundation hypotheses, and broader gaps are retained in P03.2-argument.md and the standalone P03.2-paper.tex. Run python build_deliverables.py for two actual installed-pdflatex passes, and python verify_artifacts.py for artifact consistency checks. Both TeX passes returned 0; the final paper has two underfull paragraph warnings per pass and no overfull warnings. These execution checks do not verify mathematical correctness.

notes.summary: Proper projective-space factors and ordinary locally trivial projective bundles give an exact reduction of every noninvariant full-union obstacle envelope to a base envelope; the curve sector in n2 therefore supplies stage 1 in higher dimension.
notes.detailedSummary: On any good separated strict base, every full-union competitor on a projective-space bundle is constant on each compact connected projective fiber by the scalar-stable classical maximum principle. Ordinary analytic local sections descend both competitor branches, and pullback gives the converse. For an arbitrary usc obstacle F, g(x)=inf_{p^{-1}(x)}F is usc because the bundle projection is smooth and open. The raw envelopes and their usc regularizations are exactly pullbacks, including empty families. Over the boundaryless curve sector of n2, pullback preserves stage 1; over its broader sector it preserves only the proved stage 3. The exact reduction allows a base boundary, but supplies no missing positive boundary theorem.
notes.text:
Exact reduction theorem. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued. Let X be any good separated strict K-analytic space, allowing relative boundary. Let p:Y→X be a good separated projective-space bundle which is locally analytically trivial on ORDINARY open subsets, with fiber P^{m,an}, m≥1. For every usc F:Y→R∪{−∞}, define g(x)=inf_{y∈p^{-1}(x)}F(y). Then g is usc, and for the FULL LFS/semipositive-real-PL union, s_F^Y=s_g^X∘p and (s_F^Y)*=(s_g^X)*∘p, with the empty-family convention.

Proof. Every competitor h is finite continuous and classically psh by n1's checked foundations. At x, restrict it to the analytic projective-space fiber over H(x), using scalar extension and analytic pullback. This fiber is compact, connected and boundaryless. Its connectedness can be proved from its m+1 standard closed unit-polydisc domains: each is connected because a clopen partition would glue an analytic nontrivial idempotent into its Tate algebra, which is a domain; all contain (1:…:1). They cover projective space by choosing a largest homogeneous coordinate. The restricted h attains a maximum. Its maximum set is closed by continuity and open by GRc's interior local maximum principle. Connectedness makes it the whole fiber. Hence EVERY h, with no symmetry assumption, is fiberwise constant.

Write h=b∘p. On each ordinary trivializing open, restrict h along the analytic section (1:0:…:0). For the LFS branch, its finite-maxima-of-unit local expressions pull back to LFS expressions. For the semipositive real-PL branch, GJR 5.4 and 7.6 give real PL and semipositivity after pullback. These local b agree because h is fiberwise constant, and belong to the same branch globally. Conversely p*b preserves either branch. Thus the exact union families correspond, and h≤F is equivalent to b≤g.

The projection p is smooth and surjective. Berkovich's supplied IHES 1993 paper, Corollary 3.7.4, states that a smooth morphism is open. It applies to p by its ordinary local projective-space trivializations and relative affine charts. Therefore {g<t}=p({F<t}) is open for every real t, proving usc even when g=-∞. A pointwise finite F may have fiber infimum -∞; the argument does not exclude it. The competitor correspondence proves raw equality, including both-empty families.

For any continuous open surjection p and raw extended function a, (a∘p)*=a*∘p. Continuity gives the upper inequality by pulling back base neighborhoods. Openness gives the lower inequality because the image of each neighborhood of a chosen lift is a base neighborhood. This neighborhood-supremum argument works also at −∞. Applying it to the exact raw identity proves regularized equality.

Consequently, if X satisfies n2's residue-field curve theorem, then for every F the full envelope on Y has ordinary stage 1, hence stage 2. Pull back the decreasing ordinary smooth sequence for the actual usc obstacle g. On p^{-1}(W), a common ordinary neighborhood, these are finite ordinary smooth functions with positive d'd'' and the correct decreasing limit. Analytic field extensions and every curve test preserve this stage by n1. If only n2's general curve hypotheses hold, this proof gives stage 3, not stage 2. Finite towers of such bundles follow by repetition; the effective obstacle remains usc at each step. Products X×P^{m,an} are included. For a normal curve base these give normal higher-dimensional spaces; the result also treats the displayed singular bijective-normalization bases.

The positive bundle conclusion uses a boundaryless base from n2. Its total space is boundaryless, since p is boundaryless and the base has no boundary. The exact reduction identity itself is valid with base boundary; it does not make an unproved curve boundary-approximation assertion. Arbitrary normal spaces, open-disc products and general proper fibrations without ordinary local sections are not covered. The reduction admits all noninvariant obstacles and competitors; proper connected fibers force descent rather than selecting an invariant subfamily.

The argument and checked applications are embedded in P03.2-argument.md and P03.2-paper.tex; source-extracts/source-provenance.json retains the literal Berkovich local-structure/openness pages. Rerun python extract_sources.py and python build_deliverables.py.

notes.summary: A fresh split-node calculation gives full-envelope failure for a continuous obstacle, on both an affinoid curve and its boundaryless interior, and in every higher dimension after projective factors. Sharp P03.2 necessity and the broader normal/geometrically-unibranch classification remain open.
notes.detailedSummary: For Z=M(K〈x,y〉/(xy)), choose a=-log|π|>0 and r=|π|. Set the obstacle to 0 on the x-branch and −a min(|y|/r,1) on the y-branch. Every full-union competitor is ≤−a on the entire y-branch by the radius-r disc Shilov maximum principle. Explicit LFS minorants h_n=max(−a,n^{-1}log|x|) on the x-branch and −a on the y-branch show that the raw envelope is 0 on the punctured x-branch and −a elsewhere. Regularization raises the node to 0 and fails the y-disc maximum principle, hence every CLD ordinal stage. The same proof works on Int(Z); n3 propagates it through projective factors. This is an exact counterexample, not sharp necessity for every branch or for normal geometry. The final deliverables and both successful TeX builds are retained; candidate remains false.
notes.text:
Fresh counterexample, with a complete full-family calculation. Let K be any complete nontrivially valued field, take π with 0<|π|<1, and put a=−log|π|>0 and r=|π|. Let Z=M(K〈x,y〉/(xy)), with node o and branches D_x,D_y. Let V be either Z or its boundaryless interior Int(Z), whose branches are open unit discs joined at o. Define f=0 on D_x∩V and f=−a min(|y|/r,1) on D_y∩V. The branch values agree at o with value 0, so f is finite continuous by the nodal gluing topology.

For every member h of the FULL LFS/semipositive-real-PL minorant union, the restriction to the closed y-disc of radius r is classically psh by the checked scalar-stable foundations in n1. This is a strict affinoid disc inside either V. Its singleton Shilov point η_r has h(η_r)≤f(η_r)=−a. The disc's Gauss seminorm dominates all point seminorms on every analytic power series, so η_r is a Shilov boundary. GRc Theorem 6.4 yields h≤−a on the whole closed r-disc, including o. Outside it, the obstacle is already −a. Thus all competitors are ≤−a on the complete y-branch.

Define h_n=max(−a,n^{-1}log|x|) on the x-branch and h_n=−a on the y-branch. Give o value −a. These are finite continuous LFS functions. On a nodal neighborhood where both branch radii are <|π|^n, they are constant −a. Away from o on the x-branch, x is a unit and h_n=n^{-1}max{−log|π^{-n}|,−log|x^{-1}|}, an ordinary local LFS expression. On the y-branch they are constant. They satisfy h_n≤f everywhere. At every punctured x-branch point, log|x| is finite and h_n→0; f gives the upper bound 0. On the y-branch every h_n attains the established upper bound −a. Hence the exact raw envelope is s=0 on (D_x∩V)\{o} and s=−a on D_y∩V, including o. Usc regularization changes only o to value 0. Its pullback to the closed y-disc has value 0 at the origin but −a at its singleton Shilov point, contradicting the psh maximum principle. It is not classically psh and lies in no CLD ordinal psh stage, since ordinary smooth curve psh functions are subharmonic and decreasing limits, including the transfinite sheaf construction, preserve this property. This verifies a branch obstruction even without relative boundary; on Z it explicitly also allows an actual domain boundary.

For V×P^{m,an} and obstacle f∘p, n3's exact full-family reduction, valid for either base V, gives the regularized envelope u∘p. Pullback along a projective-space section and the same closed y-disc violates the maximum principle. Thus this fresh obstruction persists in dimension m+1 for every m≥1. It does not use any dossier book assertion, generated theorem or review verdict.

What remains open. The sector in n2 and its projective counterparts in n3 is sufficient, not a sharp classification. Necessity of the residue-field, countability and boundarylessness assumptions is not proved. Non-smooth harmonic germs do not imply absence from stage 1 or 2. The broader curve route only gives stage 3; reducing it to ordinal stage 2 requires an additional ordinary approximation argument. Imperfect perfected-unibranch descent, positive approximation at relative-boundary points, arbitrary normal/geometrically-unibranch higher-dimensional domains and open-disc products are unresolved. No fresh proof is supplied for the dossier's nonsplit-node surface or codimension-two pinching assertions, and they were not imported. Exact scalar pullback positivity of the proved envelope is established, but enlarged scalar-extension competitor-family identities are not asserted. No continuity conclusion or P03.1/P03.3 classification is claimed. The original sharp P03.2 target therefore remains open, and candidate=false.
